title: Seaglider electric plane-boat hybrid takes flight in first public demo
summary: More than 600 guests watched the prototype vessel rise 30 feet above Narragansett Bay off Rhode Island.

title: Flock fight moves to Congress
summary: Bills in the U.S. House and Senate would restrict law enforcement’s use of automated license plate readers and withhold federal funds from communities that use the technology.

title: $467M affordable housing funding round gets LA City Council sign-off
summary: The record-breaking amount, which comes from sales taxes on high-value homes, will be used to build and preserve affordable housing.

title: NYC pied-à-terre tax rollout must start again, judge rules
summary: The Staten Island judge voided the city’s 17,000 mailed notices to homeowners. The city is expected to challenge the decision, Politico reported.

title: Court blocks FEMA from tying public safety grants to election policies
summary: The ruling clears the way for more than $200 million in funding for SWAT teams, bomb squads and other local preparedness efforts.

title: White House, DOT officials meet with transit leaders on safety and security
summary: While transit funding remains uncertain, transit agency officials cite fare evasion, disruptive riders, cybersecurity and terrorism as potential threats to riders.

title: $16B Hudson Tunnel rail project begins boring
summary: “We've taken the Trump administration to court five times … we’ve won five times,” said New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill during an event marking the start of tunneling for the embattled project.

title: Steep cuts to federal transit funding take effect Thursday
summary: Smaller communities and rural towns are "especially vulnerable” to the public transit and passenger rail cuts, according to the American Public Transportation Association.

title: Data centers are stress-testing local governments. Here are 5 strategies to rein them in.
summary: Tools including zoning and permitting can address transparency, infrastructure, community benefits and other concerns, panelists at a Southern Environmental Law Center event said.

title: With its first office-to-housing project done, Chicago advances ‘next chapter’ for its downtown
summary: The adaptive reuse project in the city's Loop has 117 mixed-income residential units. More conversions are in the pipeline.
